title: Choose the structure of Cornerstock
question: The brand kit stays. This choice is the layout: what leads the home screen on the counter computer and on the phone. Pick one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Find first
options.lineage: The counter question: "Do you have it in 15?"
options.thesis: One search field leads every screen. Type a model or a serial number and the answer is on screen before you finish.
options.viewport: Navy rail left. A large search field on top with the stock total beside it. Below: model rows with weight chips. A detail pane opens on the right. On the phone: search on top, scan button fixed at the thumb.
options.risk: Browsing the whole stock takes one more step than a full board.

raised.raise: A row that changes on another device moves in place and holds a gold mark until you have seen it.

options.label: Weight rack
options.lineage: The shop's ball wall: models down, weights across
options.thesis: The whole stock on one screen as a grid. Models are rows, weights from 16 lb to 10 lb are columns, each cell is a count.
options.viewport: Navy rail left. A grid fills the work area: model names in the first column, one column for each weight, counts in tabular numerals, empty cells quiet. A cell opens its balls on the right. On the phone: model rows with a strip of weight chips.
options.risk: A wide grid is hard on a phone. The phone version must be a different layout, not a squeezed grid.

options.label: Live ledger
options.lineage: The day book: each ball in, each ball out
options.thesis: The home screen is what happened today. Received, sold, and moved balls arrive at the top as they happen. Stock totals sit beside it.
options.viewport: Navy top bar with navigation. Left two thirds: today's movements, newest first, each with serial number, model, person, time. Right third: totals by brand and by location, and the scan button. On the phone: the feed, with scan fixed at the thumb.
options.risk: The feed is empty or slow on a quiet day, and the stock itself is one tap away.

options.label: Boarding pass and gate board
options.thesis: Stock as a board that reranks itself.
options.viewport: A board of rows ordered by time.
options.risk: Staff search for a ball. They do not watch a ranking.
options.case: Time order does not answer "do we have it". Loses on product clarity.
options.kept: A changed row moves in place and stays marked until it is seen.

options.label: Tabbed reference manual
options.thesis: Sections as a stepped tab rail.
options.viewport: A tab rail down the edge.
options.risk: Changes the palette and the controls, which are fixed.
options.case: Needs its own colors and unfamiliar controls. Both are outside this round.
options.kept: Changes are quick steps, not slow fades.

options.label: Gridded type specimen
options.case: Reads as an artifact first. Staff could not do the task faster.
options.kept: One strict grid across all screens.

options.label: Variable type specimen
options.viewport: One giant letter and a slider.
options.risk: No stock task maps to an axis slider.
options.case: Nothing in stock work is a continuous axis.

options.label: Dance score
options.thesis: Time read upward on a center staff.
options.case: Staff would have to learn a notation.
options.kept: Fill pattern, not color alone, shows a state.

options.label: Zoo guide map
options.thesis: Areas as lobes of flat color.
options.viewport: One green lobe across the screen.
options.risk: A new palette and playful shapes.
options.case: Replaces the confirmed palette and adds decoration.
